<translate>
A '''beam clash''' happens when two beams meet head-on. Both fighters are locked in place and a timing meter appears: every well-timed press pushes your beam forward, and the side that pushes far enough breaks through while the loser is left exhausted. Your stats matter, but timing can turn a fight around.
</translate>

<translate>
== Starting a clash ==

A clash starts when two '''beams''' fired by different fighters meet head-on. Only the Wave and Beam types clash: the Kamehameha, Galick Gun, Final Flash, Special Beam Cannon, [[Special:MyLanguage/Heat Dome Attack|Heat Dome Attack]], [[Special:MyLanguage/Mouth Blast|Mouth Blast]] and the like, Wave attacks you create yourself included. See [[Special:MyLanguage/Ki Attacks|Ki Attacks]].

Smaller attacks (Small Balls, Lasers, Disks) that run into a firing beam don't clash: they are simply destroyed.

Allies never clash with each other: party members (while party PvP is off), players on the same team and players fighting the same world boss (see [[Special:MyLanguage/World Bosses#Truce|world boss truce]]) can fire their beams side by side, and a beam doesn't destroy an ally's smaller attacks.

While the clash lasts, both fighters are held in place and '''invulnerable'''.
</translate>

<translate>
== The timing meter ==

Each fighter gets their own meter. A marker sweeps across it, changing direction on every sweep, and each sweep has a '''window''' in a different place. A sweep takes about 2 to 3 seconds.

* '''Right-click''' when the marker is inside the window.
* A press near the centre of the window is '''PERFECT'''; anywhere else inside it is '''GOOD'''.
* A press outside the window is a '''MISS''' and wastes that sweep. Only one press counts per sweep.

Presses are checked by the server, so the timing can't be faked.
</translate>

<translate>
== Pushing your beam ==

Every PERFECT or GOOD press builds '''momentum''' that pushes your beam forward: a PERFECT press gives the full amount, a GOOD press between half and the full amount depending on how close to the centre you were. Momentum fades over time, so you have to keep hitting the window.

Your stats decide how hard each press pushes: the beam with more power behind it turns the same momentum into a bigger push. A weaker fighter can still win with better timing.
</translate>

<translate>
== Winning and losing ==

The side that pushes the clash far enough '''wins''': its beam breaks through and keeps going for a moment. The losing beam is destroyed and the loser is '''exhausted''': stunned for 3.5 seconds (see [[Special:MyLanguage/Effects|Effects]]).

A clash can also end in other ways:

* If either fighter stops firing, the clash dissolves with no winner.
* If neither fighter presses for 7 seconds, the clash dissolves.
* After 30 seconds, whoever is ahead wins. If the beams are exactly even, the clash dissolves.
</translate>

<translate>
== Clashing with enemies ==

Enemies that fire beams can clash with you too. They press on their own, and the more powerful their beam is, the more accurate their timing gets.
</translate>

<translate>
== Strike clashes ==
</translate>
{{Main|Strike Clash}}
<translate>
Melee techniques can clash too: when two fighters rush at each other with strike attacks, their fists meet and the same timing meter decides who breaks through.
</translate>
